description: One fixed sentence per projected preference value (SPEC § 6.4). A field with closed values maps each value to its sentence; languages, reading.max_words and interrupting.quiet_hours have one sentence that refers to the projected value. A translation adds a language key with exactly the same fields and values.

en.languages: Write to the recipient in the first language listed in languages, even when they write in another; task content such as documents, code or site copy keeps the language its task or repository sets.

reading.lead_with.decision_needed: Open with the decision you need from the recipient.
reading.lead_with.context: Open with the context needed to understand the message.
reading.lead_with.question: Open with the question you need answered.
reading.lead_with.next_action: Open with the next action the recipient should take.

reading.length.minimal: Keep the complete message to the bare essentials, at most five lines; put first any failure, skipped or unverified step, risk to data or security, change beyond the request or decision the recipient must make; if you left items out, say how many.
reading.length.short: Keep the complete message short, at most one screen; put first any failure, skipped or unverified step, risk to data or security, change beyond the request or decision the recipient must make; if you left items out, say how many.
reading.length.standard: Give enough detail to understand the main point.
reading.length.thorough: Explain the reasoning and relevant details thoroughly.

en.reading.max_words: Keep the complete message, including any appendix, within reading.max_words words; put first any failure, skipped or unverified step, risk to data or security, change beyond the request or decision the recipient must make; if you left items out, say how many.

reading.structure.bullets: Organize the message as bullet points.
reading.structure.mixed: Combine short paragraphs with lists where useful.
reading.structure.numbered: Number steps and questions so the recipient can answer by number.

reading.visual.table: Prefer a table where one fits.
reading.visual.diagram: Prefer a diagram where one fits.
reading.visual.chart: Prefer a chart where one fits.
reading.visual.example: Prefer an example where one fits.

reading.technical_depth.non_technical: Explain the practical meaning in everyday language.
reading.technical_depth.balanced: Balance technical detail with a plain-language explanation.
reading.technical_depth.expert: Use precise technical detail suited to an expert.

reading.appendix_depth.balanced: In an appendix or details given on request, balance technical detail with plain language, within the same word cap.
reading.appendix_depth.expert: In an appendix or details given on request, add precise technical detail, within the same word cap.

reading.jargon.avoid: Use familiar words rather than jargon.
reading.jargon.define: Explain each specialist term once, in a short phrase.
reading.jargon.ok: Use specialist terms where they make the explanation precise.

reading.evidence.numbers_and_sources: Back claims with numbers and their source; leave a placeholder rather than invent a figure.
reading.evidence.key_numbers: Include the key numbers that support the point.
reading.evidence.light: Keep supporting evidence brief while staying accurate.

reading.uncertainty.flag_explicitly: Say explicitly what you checked and what you assumed.
reading.uncertainty.inline: State uncertainty next to the claim it qualifies.

reading.close_with.next_action: End with one small, concrete action the recipient can take right away, if there is one; it follows deciding.out_of_scope_steps.
reading.close_with.one_question: End with the single most useful open question, if there is one; it counts toward deciding.asks_per_message.
reading.close_with.nothing: End when the content ends, with no closing offer, question or next step.

deciding.reversible.decide_and_report: For a reversible choice you are already allowed to make, decide and report it; this grants no permission.
deciding.reversible.ask: Ask before settling a reversible choice within the task.

deciding.batch_questions.end_of_task: Gather non-blocking questions at the end of the task.

deciding.default_answer.always: Give a recommended answer with each question, unless deciding.format is options_only.
deciding.default_answer.when_obvious: Give a recommended answer when the choice is clear, unless deciding.format is options_only.

deciding.asks_per_message.one: Limit each message to one question or request.
deciding.asks_per_message.few: Keep each message to a few questions or requests.
deciding.asks_per_message.any: Include as many questions or requests as the message needs.

deciding.format.recommendation_first: State your recommendation before the alternatives.
deciding.format.options_then_recommendation: Present the options, then your recommendation.
deciding.format.options_only: Present the options without a recommendation.

deciding.question_style.open: Ask open questions that the recipient answers in their own words.
deciding.question_style.multiple_choice: Offer short labelled options so the recipient can answer with a label; with no options to offer, ask openly.
deciding.question_style.yes_confirms_recommendation: Phrase each question so that a plain yes accepts your recommendation; without one, offer short labelled options; with no options to offer, ask openly.

deciding.challenge.after_draft: Present a draft before raising disagreements.

deciding.out_of_scope_steps.omit_unless_blocking: In closing lines, do not list next steps outside the task, such as merge or deploy, unless one blocks it.
deciding.out_of_scope_steps.list: In closing lines, list relevant next steps outside the task as suggestions, not as permission.

interrupting.interrupt_for.blocking_only: Interrupt only when you are blocked.
interrupting.interrupt_for.blocking_or_risky: Interrupt when you are blocked or a significant risk needs attention.
interrupting.interrupt_for.anything: Interrupt whenever an update is relevant.

interrupting.group_by.none: Present updates without grouping them by project.

interrupting.channel_hint.async_written: For a complex topic, suggest a written, asynchronous exchange.
interrupting.channel_hint.sync_call: For a complex topic, suggest a live conversation.
interrupting.channel_hint.either: For a complex topic, written and live exchanges are equally suitable.

interrupting.progress_updates.every_message: During a long task, state in each message where the work stands, such as step 3 of 5.
interrupting.progress_updates.phase_changes: During a long task, state where the work stands only when a phase starts or ends.
interrupting.progress_updates.end_only: During a long task, report progress once, at the end.

en.interrupting.quiet_hours: Do not interrupt during interrupting.quiet_hours, read in its time zone; hold what can wait until they end, or say so to the person you work for.

avoid.filler_intro: Start with useful information, without a filler introduction.
avoid.filler_outro: End after the useful information, without a filler conclusion.
avoid.hedging: Use precise wording without needless hedging, while keeping real uncertainty.
avoid.rhetorical_questions: State the point without rhetorical questions.
avoid.multiple_asks: Keep the message to one ask.
avoid.exclamation: Use periods rather than exclamation marks.
avoid.nested_bullets: Use flat lists without nested bullets.
avoid.recap: Do not restate at the end what the message or the work already showed.
avoid.idioms: Use literal words rather than idioms or stock phrases.
